title: Code of Hammurabi
date: c. 1750 BCE (Circa 1753–1754 BCE (towards the end of Hammurabi's reign)
text: One of the oldest, most complete, and best-preserved written collections of laws in human history.

title: The Iliad
text: An ancient Greek epic poem attributed to Homer, exploring the human cost of war, grief, and the possibility of compassion between enemies.

title: Ashoka’s Dhamma
text: A set of moral and political principles promoted by Emperor Ashoka through royal edicts across the Mauryan Empire, emphasising non-violence, religious tolerance, ethical governance, and the welfare of people and animals.

title: Huquq ul-Ibad
text: An Islamic legal concept referring to the duties and responsibilities that people owe to each other or mankind in general, traditionally distinguished from the rights of God (Huqūq Allāh).

title: Maqasid al-Shari`ah / Five Principles of Shari`ah
text: A framework in Islamic jurisprudence identifying the higher objectives of Islamic law, traditionally including the protection of religion, life, intellect, lineage, and property.

title: Magna Carta
text: Established the principle that the king and his government was not above the law.

title: Genocides against Indigenous peoples
text: Colonial expansion led to widespread violence, dispossession, and the destruction of Indigenous communities, including acts of genocide across different regions and periods.

title: Colonisation of Americas
text: European colonisation of the Americas led to the dispossession and oppression of Indigenous peoples, shaping later struggles for land rights, sovereignty, reparations, and self-determination.

title: Treaty of Tordesillas / redistribution of colonised territories referenced
text: An agreement between Spain and Portugal dividing their claims to newly discovered territories outside Europe, without the consent of Indigenous peoples living there.

title: Bartolomé de las Casas and the Valladolid Debate (16th-century Spanish priest)
text: A Spanish priest who challenged the oppression and enslavement of Indigenous peoples in the Americas and defended their rights against colonial exploitation.

title: British colonisation in India
text: Beginning with the East India Company's trading activities in the 17th century, British expansion gradually developed into colonial rule, shaping later struggles for independence and self-determination.

title: Queen Nzinga’s resistance to Portuguese colonialism
text: Queen Nzinga led military and diplomatic resistance against Portuguese colonial expansion, defending the independence and sovereignty of Ndongo and Matamba.

title: U.S. Constitution
text: Established the framework of the U.S. federal government, defining its powers and introducing a system of checks and balances.

title: Haitian Revolution
text: A successful revolution against French colonial rule and slavery, leading to Haiti's independence in 1804 and challenging colonial systems of enslavement and racial domination.

title: Eugenio Espejo - Ecuador Emancipation
text: An Enlightenment thinker and writer whose criticism of colonial authorities helped inspire later movements for independence in present-day Ecuador.

title: Anglo-Nepalese War
text: A war between Nepal and the British East India Company that ended with the Treaty of Sugauli in 1816, forcing Nepal to cede territory while retaining its independence.cts the impact of colonial expansion and imperial power on political communities

title: Seneca Falls Convention
text: A landmark women's rights convention in the United States that adopted the Declaration of Sentiments, calling for women's equality and rights, including the right to vote.

title: Sepoy Mutiny / Indian Rebellion of 1857
text: A major uprising by Indian soldiers, civilians, and local rulers against British East India Company rule, challenging British colonial power in India.

title: The criminalisation of gender plurality by British colonial authorities
text: British colonial authorities used the Criminal Tribes Act of 1871 to police and criminalise Hijra communities, imposing restrictions on gender expression and traditional ways of life.

title: Oral Traditions, Storytelling and Cultural Expressions
text: Oral traditions, storytelling, songs, dance, and other cultural expressions have preserved collective memory, transmitted knowledge, and provided ways for communities to express their experiences and struggles.

title: Battle of Ulundi
text: A decisive British victory over the Zulu Kingdom that ended the Anglo-Zulu War and led to the dismantling of the Zulu Kingdom's political independence.

title: Battle of Adwa
text: Ethiopian forces under Emperor Menelik II defeated the Italian colonial army, preserving Ethiopia's independence and becoming a symbol of anti-colonial resistance across Africa.

title: Samori Touré's resistance to French colonial expansion
place: West Africa (present-day Guinea, Mali and Côte d'Ivoire)
text: Samori Touré led the Wassoulou Empire's military and diplomatic 16-year resistance to French colonial expansion in West Africa until his capture in 1898.

title: The execution of Mbuya Nehanda
text: A spiritual leader who helped organise resistance against British colonial rule during the First Chimurenga (1896–1897) and she was executed by colonial authorities in 1898.

title: Independence movements from Spanish Empire
text: Independence movements across Latin America challenged Spanish colonial rule and led to the establishment of independent states during the 19th century.

title: Begum Rokeya's Sultana’s Dream
text: An early feminist speculative imagination/one of the earliest feminist writings that we have from the region.

title: Mexican Revolution
text: A major political and social revolution that challenged authoritarian rule and inequality, advancing demands for land reform, labour rights, and social justice.

title: Geneva Declaration of the Rights of the Child
text: The first international declaration recognising children's rights, establishing principles for their protection, development, and welfare.

title: Women's suffrage in Ecuador
text: Ecuador became the first country in Latin America to constitutionally recognise women's right to vote, initially limited to literate women.

title: Kashmir uprising of 1931
text: A wave of protests against the rule of Maharaja Hari Singh, driven by grievances over political exclusion, discrimination, and demands for greater rights and representation.

title: Ethnic cleansing in Palestine
text: Since the Nakba of 1948, Palestinians have faced continued displacement, dispossession, violence and genocide.

title: Indonesian independence and new constitution
text: Indonesia declared independence from Dutch colonial rule in 1945 and adopted a new constitution, establishing the foundations of an independent republic based on sovereignty and social justice.

title: Apartheid in South Africa
text: A system of racial segregation and discrimination rooted in colonial rule, involving land dispossession, forced removals, segregation, and state violence against South Africa’s Black population.

title: Civil rights movement in the US
text: A major movement against racial segregation and discrimination in the United States, advocating for equal rights, racial justice, and political participation, particularly for African Americans.

title: Bandung Conference
text: Brought together 29 Asian and African countries to promote decolonisation, self-determination, and international solidarity, laying the foundations for the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: Martin Luther King Jr.’s 'I Have a Dream' speech
text: Once a controversial and widely opposed figure, Martin Luther King Jr. later became a celebrated symbol of racial equality.

title: Civil Rights Act of 1964
text: A landmark law emerging from the Civil Rights Movement that prohibited racial segregation in public places and discrimination in employment, advancing civil rights and equality in the United States.

title: Chipko movement
text: A grassroots environmental movement in India in which local communities, particularly women, resisted commercial deforestation through non-violent protests.

title: Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action
text: Vienna Declaration reaffirmed the universality, indivisibility, and interdependence of human rights, strengthening the post-Cold War international human rights framework.

title: Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda
text: The systematic killing of approximately 800,000 people, predominantly Tutsi, exposed the international community's failure to prevent genocide and prompted developments in international criminal accountability.

title: Indonesia's Reformasi Movement
text: A people-led reform movement that challenged authoritarian rule, leading to President Suharto's resignation in 1998 and paving the way for democratic transition.

title: South African Constitution
text: Adopted following the end of apartheid, South Africa's 1996 Constitution established a democratic framework grounded in human dignity, equality, and fundamental rights, including protections against racial discrimination.

title: Authoritarian Dictatorships in Latin America
text: Military dictatorships across Latin America used torture, enforced disappearances, and political repression gave rise to human rights movements demanding justice, and accountability.

title: UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD)
text: Adopted by the UN in 2006, CRPD established an international legal framework for disability rights, promoting equality, inclusion, accessibility, and the full participation of persons with disabilities in society.

title: UN system reform / Establishment of the UN Human Rights Council
text: The United Nations replaced its Commission on Human Rights with the Human Rights Council, aiming to strengthen international human rights protection and accountability.

title: UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP)
text: The Declaration recognised Indigenous peoples' individual and collective rights, including self-determination, cultural identity, and rights to their lands and resources.

title: Death of Alan Kurdi and global movement for rights of refugees
text: The death of three-year-old Syrian refugee Alan Kurdi and the global circulation of his photograph drew international attention to the refugee crisis, sparking public outrage and calls for greater protection of refugees.

title: April uprising in Nicaragua
text: Mass protests against government policies grew into a nationwide movement demanding democratic freedoms and human rights, met with violent repression by state security forces and pro-government groups.

title: Fridays for Future Movement
text: A youth-led climate movement that began with school strikes in Sweden in 2018 and grew into global protests demanding urgent climate action and justice for present and future generations.

title: UN Disability Inclusion Strategy (UNDIS)
text: Launched in 2019, the UN Disability Inclusion Strategy aimed to strengthen disability inclusion, accessibility, and accountability across the UN system.

title: Recognition of Same-Sex Marriage in Nepal
text: Nepal's Supreme Court ordered the registration of same-sex marriages in 2023, leading to the country's first officially registered same-sex marriage and marking a significant step towards marriage equality.

title: Global Movement Against the Genocide in Gaza
text: A global solidarity movement mobilising millions of people to protest Israel's violence in Gaza, demand an end to the genocide and blockade, and defend Palestinian rights and self-determination.

title: Recognition of the Cauca River as a Victim of Armed Conflict
text: Colombia's Special Jurisdiction for Peace recognised the Cauca River as a rights-bearing entity and a victim of armed conflict, expanding legal recognition beyond humans to nature itself.

title: Liberation Theology and the Preferential Option for the Poor
text: A religious movement that emerged in Latin America, linking Christian faith with struggles against poverty, inequality, and oppression, and emphasising justice for the poor and marginalised.

title: Argentine Economic Crisis
text: A severe economic crisis involving bank withdrawal restrictions, rising poverty, and unemployment, which sparked mass protests and exposed the social consequences of economic instability.

title: 2003 Invasion of Iraq
text: The US-led invasion of Iraq, launched without explicit UN Security Council authorisation, raised major questions about the legality of military intervention and its consequences for civilians.

title: Nepalese Civil War (Maoist Insurgency)
text: A decade-long armed conflict between Maoist rebels and Nepal's government caused widespread violence, displacement, and human rights abuses, ending with a peace agreement in 2006.

title: 2014 Gaza War
text: The 2014 war in Gaza caused widespread civilian deaths, displacement, and destruction, raising serious concerns about civilian protection and violations of international humanitarian law.

title: Anti-Muslim Discrimination and Violence in India
text: Since 2017, reports of anti-Muslim violence, hate speech, and discriminatory government practices have raised serious concerns about religious freedom, equality, and minority rights in India.

title: Protests Against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA)
text: Nationwide protests against India's Citizenship Amendment Act raised concerns about religious discrimination, citizenship rights, and the exclusion of Muslims.

title: Revocation of Jammu and Kashmir's Special Constitutional Status
text: India's removal of Jammu and Kashmir's special constitutional status was accompanied by communication shutdowns, detentions, and restrictions on movement, raising serious concerns about civil liberties and political autonomy.

title: Lebanese Financial and Economic Crisis
text: Lebanon's financial crisis led to the loss of savings, widespread poverty, and mass protests, exposing the consequences of economic collapse for people's livelihoods and social rights.

title: Online Harassment of Muslim Women in India
text: The Sulli Deals and Bulli Bai apps used photographs of Muslim women in fake online auctions, exposing gendered Islamophobia, online harassment, and discrimination.

title: Prem Prasad Acharya's Suicide and Protests in Nepal
text: The suicide of Prem Prasad Acharya and following a public act of protest sparked demonstrations in Nepal and drew attention to economic hardship, government accountability, and social injustice.

title: Digital Witnessing and Documentation of the Genocide in Gaza
text: Palestinians in Gaza have used social media and digital platforms to document and share the violence and destruction they experience, enabling people worldwide to witness the atrocities and mobilise in solidarity.

title: Indigenous Resistance to the Maya Train Project
text: Indigenous communities in Mexico have challenged the Maya Train development project over concerns about land rights, environmental damage, and inadequate consultation, defending their territories and right to self-determination.

title: Ingëd (Ancestral Land), Këgëëtëwon (Identity), Këgëbaya-baya (Self-determination)
text: Indigenous concepts connecting ancestral land, cultural identity, and collective self-determination.

title: Ruray Fusaka (Treasures in the Domains)
text: A Teduray and Lambangian hymn celebrating ancestral lands, cultural identity, and collective resistance, expressing Indigenous communities' determination to protect their territories.

title: Qur'an 8:9, Divine Support in Times of Conflict
text: “Remember when you cry to your Lord for help He answered 'I will refinforce you with a thousand angels'.” Qur’an 8:9 -- A Qur'anic verse recalling a plea for divine help during the Battle of Badr, expressing themes of faith, hope, and support in times of conflict.

title: Henry David Thoreau, “Civil Disobedience”
text: An influential essay arguing that individuals should follow their conscience and refuse to cooperate with unjust government policies, particularly slavery and war.

title: Amar Hath Bandhibi Fao Bandhibi (collected from unknown rural indigenous woman)
text: "Amar Haat Bandhibi" (আমার হাত বান্ধিবি) is a famous traditional Bengali folk song that questions how physical restraints can stop a person's mind or soul from feeling deep love and longing. The line "Mon bandhibi kemone?" asks, "How will you tie down my mind?"

title: Viktor Frankl, Man's Search for Meaning
text: A memoir by Holocaust survivor Viktor Frankl exploring the search for meaning, human dignity, and psychological resilience in the face of extreme suffering. “We cannot control what happens to us, but can control our responses.”

title: Jail Journal by Bishweshwar Prasad (BP) Koirala
text: A prison diary by Nepal's former Prime Minister B. P. Koirala, reflecting on political imprisonment, democracy, and his struggle against authoritarian rule.

title: Garibako Chameli
text: "Garibako Chameli" is a famous Nepali revolutionary folk song that highlights social inequality and the struggles of ordinary people. Its famous refrain means "there is no one to speak up for the poor".

title: Camelamos Naquerar
text: Camelamos Naquerar (meaning "We Want to Speak" in Caló, the language of the Spanish Romani people) is a groundbreaking 1976 theatrical and musical work that revolutionised flamenco and became a foundational manifesto for the Spanish Roma social movement

title: Orientalism by Edward Said
text: A landmark book examining how Western representations of Eastern societies helped construct and justify colonial power and domination.

title: La Conjura - Maya Theatre and Historical Resistance
text: “La Conjura de Xinum” (often called La Conjura) is a community theater play about the Caste War of Yucatán, based on the historical novel by writer Ermilo Abreu Gómez. It retells the Maya rebellion in Yucatán from an Indigenous perspective, challenging colonial narratives and reclaiming Maya history and identity.

title: Do You Hear the People Sing? - Les Misérables
text: Originally written for the musical Les Misérables, the song became a global anthem of resistance, used by protest movements to express solidarity and demands for freedom and justice.

title: This Fissured Land: An Ecological History of India - Madhav Gadgil and Ramachandra Guha
text: A book exploring India's environmental history, examining how colonial rule, social inequalities, and different approaches to resource use have shaped relationships between people and nature.

title: Hamro Nepal Maa - Song from Balidaan
text: A song from the Nepali film Balidaan (1997), which portrays resistance to authoritarian rule and struggles for democracy and political freedom.

title: The Production of Hindu-Muslim Violence in Contemporary India - Paul R. Brass
text: A book examining how Hindu-Muslim violence in India can be deliberately organised and sustained by political and institutional actors.

title: Sachar Committee Report
text: A government-commissioned report documenting inequalities faced by Muslim communities in India, particularly in education, employment, and economic opportunities, and calling for greater equality and inclusion.

title: Desaparesidos - Lualhati Bautista
text: A novel exploring enforced disappearances, political repression, and the lasting impact of martial law on families during the Marcos dictatorship in the Philippines.

title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do? by Michael Sandel
text: A book exploring different ideas of justice, equality, and individual rights, encouraging critical reflection on moral and political questions in society.

title: We Teach Life, Sir! - Rafeef Ziadah
text: A spoken-word poem challenging the dehumanisation of Palestinians and media representations of their suffering, while expressing Palestinian resilience, dignity, and resistance.

title: Fire in the Blood - Dylan Mohan Gray
text: A documentary exposing how pharmaceutical patents and corporate interests restricted access to affordable HIV/AIDS medicines, highlighting global inequalities in the right to health.

title: Gujarat Files: Anatomy of a Cover Up - Rana Ayyub
text: An investigative book examining allegations of state complicity in the 2002 Gujarat riots and extrajudicial killings, highlighting the role of journalism in exposing human rights abuses and demanding accountability.

title: Bagong Bayani - Dicta License (feat. Ja Quintana)
text: A Filipino protest song calling on people to speak out against injustice and oppression, promoting freedom, peace, and collective responsibility.

title: Tarian Penghancur Raya by .Feast
text: An Indonesian protest song criticising environmental destruction and the loss of traditional cultures, highlighting the impact of human activities on nature and local communities.

title: The Seed by Aurora
text: "The Seed" by Norwegian artist AURORA is a powerful environmental anthem about human greed, climate change, and our destructive relationship with the planet.

title: Recognise, Resist, Rebuild: A Manifesto for Palestinian Liberation and Ecological Justice
text: This Manifesto calls for recognising that climate justice is inseparable from ending occupation, apartheid, genocide, and ecocide.

title: Otros Futuros
text: Otros Futuros is a participatory card and tabletop game created by a Latin American collective that invites groups and communities to imagine and co-create a thriving world beyond the current planetary crisis.

title: Resistance songs through the Mesoamerican caravan journey
text: Migrants travelling through Mexico used songs and collective chants to express solidarity, resist discrimination, and demand dignity and protection of their rights.

title: Mëntëfëwalëy - Indigenous Teduray Understandings of Gender
text: The Indigenous Teduray concept of Mëntëfëwalëy recognises diverse gender identities, challenging colonial and Western assumptions about gender and affirming Indigenous understandings of identity and belonging.

title: Establishment of the Department of Orang Asli
text: Established under British colonial rule, the department aimed to protect and administer Orang Asli communities, while also extending state control over their lives, lands, and autonomy.

title: Assassination of Patrice Lumumba
text: Patrice Lumumba, the first Prime Minister of independent Congo, was assassinated amid political struggles, a conspiracy of Western powers and local rivals to prevent Soviet influence and preserve foreign control over the Congo’s vast mineral wealth.

title: 1964 Calcutta Riots
text: Widespread communal violence in Calcutta, particularly targeting Muslim communities, caused deaths, displacement, and destruction, exposing continuing religious tensions.

title: Alangkat Movement (Tëduray and Lambangian Peoples)
text: An Indigenous movement by the Tëduray and Lambangian peoples to protect their ancestral territories, customary laws, and spiritual traditions against colonial interference and state control.

title: 1970 Bhiwandi Riots
text: The 1970 Bhiwandi riots were severe communal clashes between Hindus and Muslims that broke out on May 7 and 8, 1970, in the textile towns of Bhiwandi, Jalgaon, and Mahad in Maharashtra, India. Communal violence in Maharashtra disproportionately affected Muslim communities, causing deaths and destruction and exposing religious discrimination and police failures to protect minorities.

title: Naxalbari uprising
text: An armed peasant uprising against land inequality and exploitation in West Bengal, which gave rise to the Naxalite movement and wider struggles over land rights and social justice.

title: Hum Dekhenge — Faiz Ahmad Faiz / Iqbal Bano
text: “Hum Dekhenge” is a famous revolutionary Urdu poem that became an global anthem of resistance against military dictatorship and political oppression.

title: 1980 Moradabad Riots
text: Communal violence in Moradabad began with a confrontation between police and Muslim worshippers during Eid prayers, resulting in deaths, further violence, and serious concerns about police conduct and minority protection.

title: Nellie Massacre
text: The mass killing of Bengali-origin Muslims in Assam during political unrest over immigration and citizenship, exposing ethnic and religious violence and failures of state protection.

title: Hashimpura Massacre
text: Members of India's Provincial Armed Constabulary detained and killed 38 Muslim men during communal unrest in Meerut, exposing targeted state violence and failures of minority protection.

title: 1989 Bhagalpur Riots
text: Widespread communal violence in Bhagalpur killed hundreds of people, predominantly Muslims, and displaced thousands, exposing religious discrimination and failures of state protection.

title: Demolition of the Babri Masjid
text: The Babri Masjid, a 16th-century mosque in the Indian city of Ayodhya, was destroyed by a large group of activists of the Vishva Hindu Parishad and allied organisations. The mosque had been the subject of a lengthy socio-political dispute, and was targeted after a political rally organised by Hindu nationalist organisations turned violent.

title: 2002 Gujarat Violence
text: Following a deadly train fire in Godhra, widespread violence in Gujarat disproportionately targeted Muslim communities, causing mass killings, displacement, and destruction, and raising serious concerns about state accountability.

title: Bolsa Família Programme
text: Launched in Brazil in 2003, Bolsa Família provided financial support to low-income families, helping reduce poverty and inequality while encouraging access to education and healthcare.

title: 2006 Malegaon Bombings
text: A series of bombings near a mosque and cemetery in Malegaon killed 31 people, mostly Muslim worshippers, raising serious concerns about religious violence and the failure to deliver justice to victims.

title: 2008 Assam Serial Bombings
text: A series of coordinated bombings across Assam killed dozens of civilians and injured hundreds, highlighting the human cost of armed violence and the need for civilian protection and accountability.

title: 2013 Muzaffarnagar Riots
text: Widespread communal violence in Uttar Pradesh killed more than 60 people, mostly Muslims, and displaced tens of thousands, exposing religious tensions and failures of state protection.

title: Niyamgiri Judgment / Dongria Kondh vs Vedanta
text: The 2013 Niyamgiri Supreme Court ruling gave the indigenous Dongria Kondh community the final legal authority to decide on Vedanta Resources' proposed bauxite mining project in the sacred Niyamgiri Hills of Odisha, India. A landmark Indigenous-rights struggle linking ancestral land, cultural and religious rights, environmental protection and community consent.

title: Lynching of Mohsin Shaikh
text: Mohsin Shaikh, a young Muslim man, was killed by a mob during communal unrest in Pune, highlighting anti-Muslim violence and the struggle for justice and accountability.

title: 2015 Dimapur Mob Lynching
text: A mob broke into a prison in Dimapur and killed Syed Farid Khan, a Muslim man accused of rape, exposing the dangers of mob violence, prejudice, and failures of state protection.

title: Disappearance of Najeeb Ahmed
text: Najeeb Ahmed's 2016 disappearance highlighted intense ideological polarisation on Indian campuses, sparked nationwide protests regarding minority student safety, and raised significant concerns about the accountability of national investigative agencies.

title: Citizenship Amendment Act and Anti-CAA Protests
text: The passage of India's Citizenship Amendment Act sparked nationwide protests over religious discrimination, citizenship rights, and fears that its interaction with citizenship verification processes could disproportionately exclude Muslims.

title: 2020 Delhi Communal Violence
text: Communal violence in northeast Delhi, following protests against India's citizenship laws, killed 53 people, predominantly Muslims, and exposed serious concerns about religious discrimination, police conduct, and state accountability.

title: Movement to Reform Thailand's Lèse-Majesté Law (Section 112)
text: Emerging prominently during Thailand's youth-led pro-democracy protests in 2020, the movement challenged the use of Section 112 to prosecute criticism of the monarchy and called for legal reform, freedom of expression, and democratic accountability.

title: “Bulldozer Justice” and Punitive Demolitions in Indi
text: Demolitions of predominantly Muslim-owned homes and businesses, including in Khargone (2022) and Nuh (2023), raised serious concerns about collective punishment, religious discrimination, housing rights, and due process.

title: Kenya's Gen Z Protests
text: Youth-led protests against Kenya's proposed tax increases grew into nationwide demands for economic justice and government accountability, prompting the withdrawal of the Finance Bill amid deadly police repression.

title: Mesoamerican Caravan for Climate and Life
text: Indigenous communities, land defenders, and climate activists mobilised across Mesoamerica and South America towards COP30 in Brazil, connecting climate justice with territorial rights and resistance to extractivism.
